concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Create one polished new colour exploration of the Aboiteau logo, presented on a clean flat warm ivory background, landscape 3:2.
Input image 1 is the approved A SHAPE reference: preserve its broad silhouette, rounded apex and feet, two separate pieces, triangular counter and generous perfectly straight diagonal negative-space channel rising from left to right. Image 2 is the colour and lowercase wordmark reference only.
Direction: COLOUR-CUT A. Incorporate the brand colour swatches into the mark itself as a small number of confident flat ink areas. The upper arch stays predominantly ultramarine; the lower piece combines a broad vermilion field and a sunny yellow swatch with a little ultramarine anchoring it. One very small pink overprint accent is permitted if it improves the balance. Use asymmetric large colour regions that respond to the A's angles, not a horizontal rainbow. Colours target ultramarine #1746D1, vermilion #F04B32, yellow #F7D447, optional pink #ED5798, paper #F6EEDD, ink #212722.
Keep the silhouette as clean and legible as the approved mark. The palette must be integrated INSIDE the A, never a detached row of colour chips or decoration next to the logo. The open diagonal channel and triangular counter stay clear ivory. Crisp vector-like edges, solid flat colours, restrained geometric swatch boundaries, no brush texture in this direction.
Composition: one large standalone coloured A centred in the upper two-thirds with generous breathing room; below it a single much smaller horizontal lockup repeating the same coloured A beside the exact lowercase word "aboiteau" in sturdy clean near-black human grotesk lettering. Only one direction, not an options grid.
Text verbatim: "aboiteau". No other text. No tagline, swatch legend, hex labels, board title, frame, mockups, gradients, shadows, bevels, stars, flags, maps, maritime imagery, AI motifs, or decorative squiggles. This must feel like a usable distinctive software brand mark.

Use case: logo-brand.
Create one polished new logo exploration for Aboiteau incorporating the tactile COLOUR SWATCHES from the identity artwork into the A symbol itself. Clean flat warm ivory background, landscape 3:2.
Input image 1 is the approved A SHAPE reference and takes priority: keep the broad rounded A silhouette, its rounded apex and feet, two separate pieces, triangular opening and generous completely straight rising diagonal negative-space channel. Input image 2 supplies the energetic blue/red/yellow screenprint swatches and sturdy lowercase wordmark style, not its layout.
Direction: OVERPRINT A. Make the interior of the approved A feel printed from three or four broad asymmetric overlapping ink swatches: ultramarine is the structural main mass, an assertive vermilion sweep traverses the lower part, and a broad blunt-ended sunny yellow swatch crosses a portion of the arch; a very small pink overprint is optional. Let opaque ink fields and a few controlled overlap areas suggest physical screenprinting. Restrained ink grain and subtly rough internal swatch edges; keep the outer silhouette disciplined and the diagonal ivory cut perfectly clean and open. The swatches are clipped to the A shape and never float as unrelated decoration. No little dashes or repeated confetti. Large simple colour masses, recognisable at small size; avoid treating this as a dense artwork illustration.
Palette targets: ultramarine #1746D1, vermilion #F04B32, yellow #F7D447, tiny optional pink #ED5798, background paper #F6EEDD, wordmark ink #212722. No equal horizontal bands or flag arrangement.
Composition: one large standalone colourful A centred in the upper two-thirds, and below it one much smaller horizontal lockup of the same coloured A beside the exact lowercase word "aboiteau" in sturdy clean near-black human grotesk lettering. Plenty of empty space, precise spacing, one direction only.
Text verbatim: "aboiteau". No other text. No tagline, palette chips, legends, hex codes, labels, titles, frames, paper photograph, mockups, gradients, glow, shadows, bevels, stars, flags, maps, literal waves, boats, generic AI symbols. The result is a distinctive expressive logo, not a brand moodboard.
